title: Velocity Brief: Compact Performance Snapshot for Route & Model
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design a compact, information-dense performance snapshot card used across the Redwood Console for both per-route and per-model views. The Velocity Brief is intended as a top-line tile that surfaces latency distributions, throughput trends, token-volume signals, and cost attribution in a single glance, with tap-throughs to expanded microtraces and rollout state. It must be usable in crowded dashboard grids, embed in route detail pages, and fit as a compact column in the model catalog list. Emphasis on scannability, progressive disclosure, and consistent interaction patterns across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Compact tile renders at three sizes: tiny (120x80), standard (240x120), and expanded inline (480x200) without layout regressions
Tile shows 90th/95th latency callouts and a sparkline with selectable quantile bands
Token flow mini-waterfall displays prefix vs. generated token split and aggregates token cost per 1k tokens
Throughput axis supports 1m/5m/1h aggregation toggles; data points align with backend aggregation windows
Clicking token cost opens cost breakdown modal pre-filtered to the current route/model and time range
Canary/rollout state is visible with color-coded badges and a hover flyout showing active variant percentages
Accessibility: all interactive elements keyboard-focusable and pass WCAG AA color contrast requirements
Design handoff includes Figma frames, component tokens, and annotated chart spec table
chart_specs: Latency quantile sparkline: mini-sparkline with shaded 50/90/95 percentile bands; y-axis auto-normalizes to 99th percentile; tooltip shows exact quantiles and sample count
Throughput trendline: area chart with per-minute aggregation; secondary axis for concurrent inflight requests; hover crosshair shows raw request counts
Token waterfall microchart: stacked bar representing prefix tokens / user tokens / generated tokens for latest N requests; bars are normalized and show absolute count on hover
Cost microstack: stacked bar of CPU/GPU/IO token cost per 1k tokens with dashed goal line showing expected unit cost
Error rate mini-gauge: circular micro-gauge with last-minute error rate and a small trend sparkline
Latency distribution violin (expanded view): lightweight violin plot for selected timeframe with median/iqr/mean markers and outlier dots; click-to-open microtrace
decisions: Use compact multi-layer sparklines (quantile bands + median) instead of separate small multiples to conserve vertical space
Show cost-per-1k as primary cost metric in compact view; detailed cost-by-resource reserved for expanded modal
Embed rollout state as an inline badge with hover for percent breakdowns (avoids full row expansion)
Default time range on tile is 1h with quick toggles to 6h/24h; exploratory time ranges available in expanded view
open_questions: Should the token waterfall compute from sampled recent N requests or from aggregated bucketed counts? (engineering input required)
What API contract will provide 95th/99th quantiles with acceptable latency for live dashboards?
How should Private deployments surface KMS/obfuscated cost numbers for regulated customers who cannot display raw cost?
Is there appetite to include model-variant comparison toggles inside the compact tile, or keep that only in expanded UX?
design_notes: Prototype emphasizes progressive disclosure: tiny tiles show a single sparkline + 90th latency badge; standard tiles add throughput and token waterfall; expanded inline tiles surface violin and cost microstack. Use semantic color tokens aligned with Console palette: neutral for baseline, orange for warnings (latency regressions), red for errors, teal for rollout-active. Motion: micro-animations for sparklines (prefers reduced-motion setting).
implementation_notes: Frontend: React component 'VelocityBriefTile' with props sizeVariant (tiny|standard|expanded), timeRange, routeId/modelId, and onOpenDetail. Reuse chart primitives from telemetry-ui (Sparkline, MicroBar, Violin). Backend: new consolidated endpoint /api/v1/telemetry/compact_snapshot?entity={route|model}&id=<id>&range=<range> returning pre-aggregated quantiles, token buckets, and cost deltas. Fallback: if compact endpoint unavailable, compose tile from existing endpoints but lazy-load heavy data on hover/expand.
